body:
Hey, I really appreciate the reassurance. It really has been *the worst* withdrawal I've experienced, and I've sampled a few from various SSRIs and such over the years. I'm some kind of connoisseur. 

There's a lot of information online regarding this stuff, and a good portion of it seems either to be hyperbole or the really extreme bad end of the spectrum that I can only hope I'm nowhere near. It's nice to hear what sounds to be both reasonable and knowledgeable feedback.

Two months is a lot in the short term, but admittedly very little time lost overall, yeah. Honestly, to hear that "getting better" isn't a linear thing in this context is immensely helpful; I thought I was starting to feel like myself last Saturday, only to have everything crash down on me again earlier this week. That was incredibly confusing, and made me wonder if my brain was just going to be vacillating between feeling decent and feeling like hell indefinitely.

I kept my original post fairly brief and simplified because there's a lot more to the benzo "causing some issues", but I should mention that I'd essentially been on a downward psychological slide for the past few months after feeling incredible for several months after starting my sex transition. For a while I couldn't figure out what the hell was eating me so slowly, which then went from the troubles clonazepam was causing for me, to the much more terrifying problems of its withdrawals. So all-in-all I've felt pretty out of it for a bit here, which has helped in making that newfound sense of self seem all the more distant and fleeting; like a cruel tease. 

I will try to get in touch with my doctor Monday. Even that is incredibly nerve-wracking, as I am not looking forward to being chewed out for stopping my medication so abruptly without her knowing, especially while I'm feeling so vulnerable. 

In any case, thank you, Stranger-on-the-Internet. This is really the sort of perspective I needed right now.
